It\n4\tkeeps a dependency graph of work items (\"beads\") in SQLite, hands out exactly\n5\tone unblocked bead per request through an atomic claim, and checkpoints the\n6\twhole workspace to deterministic JSONL that Git can track.\n7\t\n8\tThe installed binary is named `bead`.\n9\t\n10\t<picture>\n11\t  <source media=\"(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)\" srcset=\"docs/img/bead-lifecycle-static.png\">\n12\t  <img alt=\"Six stages of the bead-rs lifecycle. Three beads are created; a blocks edge makes store wait on design; design and docs are ready while store is blocked; a worker claims design, which becomes in progress; closing design satisfies the edge and store becomes ready; a flush copies SQLite to the checkpoint.\" src=\"docs/img/bead-lifecycle.gif\">\n13\t</picture>\n14\t\n15\t*The animation plays twice and stops. If your system asks for reduced motion\n16\tyou get the [static storyboard](docs/img/bead-lifecycle-static.png) instead,\n17\twhich shows the same six stages.*\n18\t\n19\tWork items form a directed acyclic graph. The **ready frontier** is the set of\n20\tbeads with nothing left blocking them — open, unassigned, not manually blocked,\n21\tand with every `blocks` edge already closed. Agents call `bead claim`, which\n22\tselects from that frontier and assigns the bead in a single transaction, so\n23\tconcurrent claimants never receive the same bead. Closing a bead can expose its\n24\tdependents, which advances the frontier.\n25\t\n26\t## Install\n27\t\n28\t```bash\n29\tcargo install --path .          # installs the `bead` binary\n30\tbead --version\n31\t```\n32\t\n33\tRequires Rust 1.75 or newer. SQLite is bundled; there is no system dependency\n34\tand no network access at runtime.\n35\t\n36\t## Quick start\n37\t\n38\t```bash\n39\tbead init --prefix demo\n40\t\n41\tdesign=$(bead create --title \"Design schema\" --priority 1)\n42\tstore=$(bead create --title \"Implement store\" --priority 2)\n43\tbead create --title \"Write docs\" --priority 3\n44\t\n45\t# `store` cannot start until `design` is closed.\n46\tbead dep add \"$store\" \"$design\"\n47\t\n48\tbead list --ready                       # design + docs; store is blocked\n49\tbead claim --assignee worker-1          # atomically takes the highest-priority ready bead\n50\tbead close \"$design\" --reason \"Schema agreed\"\n51\tbead list --ready                       # store has now joined the frontier\n52\t\n53\tbead sync flush-only                    # idempotent check; publishes nothing new\n54\t```\n55\t\n56\t![Terminal recording of the quick start: init, three beads, a dependency, the ready frontier, a claim, a close, and a checkpoint flush](docs/img/bead-workflow.gif)\n57\t\n58\tThat recording is the sequence above, run against the real binary — note that\n59\t`store` is absent from the first `list --ready` because it is blocked, and\n60\tpresent in the second because closing `design` satisfied its only edge.\n61\t\n62\t`bead why --id <ID>` explains any bead's state: whether it is ready, what is\n63\tblocking it, how it ranks for claiming, and which operations are currently\n64\tlegal.\n65\t\n66\t## State model\n67\t\n68\tTwo artifacts, with different jobs:\n69\t\n70\t| Path | Role | Committed |\n71\t| --- | --- | --- |\n72\t| `.beads/beads.db` | SQLite, authoritative live state | No |\n73\t| `.beads/checkpoint/` | Deterministic JSONL checkpoint | Yes |\n74\t\n75\tThe checkpoint carries issues, the event history, provenance receipts, and the\n76\tdependency and label graph. **Every successful mutation publishes it\n77\tautomatically** after its transaction commits, so it is never silently behind\n78\tthe database and a clone of the repository reproduces the current state.\n79\t`bead sync flush-only` remains an explicit idempotent check — against a\n80\tcurrent checkpoint it publishes nothing and exits 0 — and `--no-auto-flush` or\n81\t`checkpoint.auto_flush: false` in `.beads/config.json` suppresses automatic\n82\tpublication, leaving the checkpoint to be advanced by that explicit command.\n83\t\n84\tRecovering a fresh clone, which arrives with a checkpoint but no database:\n85\t\n86\t```bash\n87\tbead init\n88\tbead sync import-only --input .beads/checkpoint --restore-into-empty --actor \"$USER\"\n89\tbead doctor\n90\t```\n91\t\n92\t`bead doctor` runs read-only integrity checks across store, backup, schema,\n93\tdependencies, and comments; `--repair` performs only safe, non-speculative\n94\trepairs, and `--rehearse` proves the recovery path by restoring into a throwaway\n95\tworkspace and comparing the result for semantic equivalence.\n96\t\n97\t## Output contracts\n98\t\n99\t- `--json` on `list`, `changes`, and `query --output-json` emits **NDJSON** —\n100\t  one compact object per line, not a JSON array.\n101\t- `bead show --json` emits a **one-element array**, which is what NEEDLE's\n102\t  subprocess contract expects.\n103\t- `bead create` prints only the new bead ID and a newline, so it can be captured\n104\t  directly into a shell variable.\n105\t- `bead claim` on an empty frontier is success, not failure: exit 0 with `{}`.\n106\t- `bead capabilities` emits a machine-readable contract document for feature\n107\t  negotiation.\n108\t\n109\tExit codes are stable across every command:\n110\t\n111\t| Code | Meaning |\n112\t| --- | --- |\n113\t| 0 | Success |\n114\t| 1 | Internal failure |\n115\t| 2 | CLI usage or validation error |\n116\t| 3 | Workspace, issue, or file not found |\n117\t| 4 | Conflict — invalid transition, revision guard, dependency cycle, single-claim refusal |\n118\t| 5 | Malformed input or integrity failure |\n119\t\n120\t## Coordinating a fleet\n121\t\n122\t![Many agents claiming from one ready frontier, backed by SQLite and a checkpoint](docs/img/how-bead-rs-works.png)\n123\t\n124\t- **Atomic claim.** Selection and assignment share one transaction under the\n125\t  `fifo-v1` policy (priority ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC). `aging-v1`,\n126\t  `impact-v1`, `rotation-v1`, and `balanced-v1` are also available via\n127\t  `--policy`.\n128\t- **Leases.** `bead claim --lease-ttl SECONDS` issues a lease with a\n129\t  monotonically increasing fencing token, so a crashed or partitioned worker\n130\t  cannot mutate work that has since been reassigned.\n131\t- **Single-claim guard.** `bead claim --single-claim` refuses the claim when\n132\t  the assignee already holds an `in_progress` issue in the workspace, failing\n133\t  with exit 4 and reason code `assignee_has_active_claim` naming the blocking\n134\t  issue. Opt-in per call, like `--lease-ttl`; it bounds claim accumulation but\n135\t  does not detect stale claims — combine it with a lease TTL to bound how long\n136\t  an abandoned claim can persist.\n137\t- **Revision guards.** `--if-revision N` on `update`, `release`, `close`, and\n138\t  `reopen` gives optimistic concurrency control; a stale revision fails with\n139\t  exit 4 rather than silently losing an update.\n140\t- **Inspect without reserving.** `bead list --ready` uses the same ordering as\n141\t  `claim` but takes nothing off the frontier.\n142\t- **Change feed.** `bead changes --since <CURSOR>` lets a consumer catch up\n143\t  incrementally instead of rescanning.\n144\t\n145\t## Interoperability\n146\t\n147\tbead-rs keeps a private native schema. Per [ADR-002](docs/adr/002-agent-guided-rehydration-over-cross-tool-migration.md)\n148\tit does not parse or transform another tool's checkpoint format:\n149\t\n150\t- `native-v1` — full fidelity, the default; the only supported recovery format\n151\t- `needle-v1` — NEEDLE subprocess compatibility\n152\t\n153\t`bead compare --id <ID> --source <P> --target <P>` reports which fields a\n154\tgiven profile pair preserves, transforms, omits, or cannot represent, scoped\n155\tto these two profiles. Moving existing work from another tracker is\n156\t**agent-guided rehydration**, not import: an agent reads the source\n157\trepository read-only and recreates work through public `bead` commands,\n158\tproducing a reconciliation report rather than a synthesized checkpoint. See\n159\t[interoperability notes](docs/notes/interoperability-architecture.md) and\n160\t[NEEDLE compatibility](docs/notes/needle-compatibility.md).\n161\t\n162\t## CLI conventions worth knowing\n163\t\n164\tbead-rs is an independent implementation, not a drop-in replacement for any\n165\tother task tracker. These conventions catch people out:\n166\t\n167\t| | |\n168\t| --- | --- |\n169\t| The binary is `bead` | not the crate name `bead-rs` |\n170\t| `create` takes a flag | `bead create --title \"Title\"`, not a positional title |\n171\t| Ready work is a filter | `bead list --ready`, not a `ready` command |\n172\t| `flush-only` is a subcommand | `bead sync flush-only`, not `bead sync --flush-only` |\n173\t| `--json` emits NDJSON | one object per line, not an array (except `show`, which emits a one-element array) |\n174\t\n175\t## Documentation\n176\t\n177\t- `bead --help` for the command inventory; `bead <COMMAND> --help` for the full\n178\t  description, examples, and semantics of any command.\n179\t- Man pages covering the whole command tree (45 pages, named `bead.1`,\n180\t  `bead-create.1`, `bead-sync-flush-only.1`, …) are generated with\n181\t  `cargo run --bin generate-man-pages`. See [MAN_PAGES.md](MAN_PAGES.md).\n182\t- The [0.1 implementation plan](docs/plan/plan.md) defines the native schema,\n183\t  lifecycle, dependency, checkpoint, CLI, and verification design.\n184\t- Post-0.1 candidates and rejected alternatives live in the\n185\t  [ideas ledger](docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md).\n186\t\n187\tBoth animations are generated from committed sources, so they can be refreshed\n188\trather than redrawn:\n189\t\n190\t```bash\n191\t# lifecycle animation (needs cairosvg + Pillow)\n192\tpython3 docs/img/generate-lifecycle-animation.py\n193\t\n194\t# terminal screencast (needs vhs, which needs ttyd + ffmpeg)\n195\tcargo install --path . && vhs docs/img/bead-workflow.tape\n196\t```\n197\t\n198\tThe screencast drives the real binary, so it cannot quietly disagree with the\n199\tCLI: if behaviour changes, re-running the tape either shows the change or\n200\tvisibly fails.\n201\t\n202\tThe lifecycle animation is timed against the classical animation principles,\n203\tused to carry meaning rather than decoration — the claim fires in 0.2s against\n204\t0.4–0.6s elsewhere because atomicity is the point, and closing `design` sends a\n205\tripple along the edge so that `store` turning ready reads as a consequence\n206\trather than a coincidence.\n207\t\n208\tIt also targets WCAG 2.1 AA. Every colour holding text clears 4.5:1 and every\n209\tmeaningful graphic clears 3:1, asserted at generation time so the palette\n210\tcannot regress; state is never colour-only, since each bead carries a text tag;\n211\tthe animation plays a fixed number of times rather than looping forever; and a\n212\t`prefers-reduced-motion` source serves the static storyboard instead. Emphasis\n213\tis carried by scale and stroke weight rather than by dimming, because a dim\n214\tdeep enough to read as staging takes text below the contrast floor. The\n215\tgenerator documents both mappings in full.\n216\t\n217\tEvery `bead ...` example printed in the help text is parsed by the real CLI in\n218\tthe test suite, so a documented invocation cannot drift from the interface it\n219\tdocuments.\n220\t\n221\t## Project status\n222\t\n223\tThe core CLI is implemented and in use: workspace lifecycle, issue CRUD,\n224\tlabels, the dependency graph, atomic and leased claims, checkpoint flush and\n225\trestore, diagnostics, the query language, the change feed, profiles, and\n226\tmigration. It has been exercised end to end by building a real multi-bead\n227\tproject through it.\n228\t\n229\tTreat it as young software rather than settled: it is a 0.1, its history\n230\tincludes bugs that a green test suite did not catch, and it is worth running\n231\t`bead doctor` and a hands-on smoke test of the path you care about before\n232\tdepending on it for anything critical.\n233\t\n234\t## Independence\n235\t\n236\t`bead-rs` has an independent Git history and is implemented from the\n237\tspecifications committed to this repository. publishes nothing new\n```\n\n![Terminal recording of the quick start: init, three beads, a dependency, the ready frontier, a claim, a close, and a checkpoint flush](docs/img/bead-workflow.gif)\n\nThat recording is the sequence above, run against the real binary — note that\n`store` is absent from the first `list --ready` because it is blocked, and\npresent in the second because closing `design` satisfied its only edge.\n\n`bead why --id <ID>` explains any bead's state: whether it is ready, what is\nblocking it, how it ranks for claiming, and which operations are currently\nlegal.\n\n## State model\n\nTwo artifacts, with different jobs:\n\n| Path | Role | Committed |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `.beads/beads.db` | SQLite, authoritative live state | No |\n| `.beads/checkpoint/` | Deterministic JSONL checkpoint | Yes |\n\nThe checkpoint carries issues, the event history, provenance receipts, and the\ndependency and label graph. **Every successful mutation publishes it\nautomatically** after its transaction commits, so it is never silently behind\nthe database and a clone of the repository reproduces the current state.\n`bead sync flush-only` remains an explicit idempotent check — against a\ncurrent checkpoint it publishes nothing and exits 0 — and `--no-auto-flush` or\n`checkpoint.auto_flush: false` in `.beads/config.json` suppresses automatic\npublication, leaving the checkpoint to be advanced by that explicit command.\n\nRecovering a fresh clone, which arrives with a checkpoint but no database:\n\n```bash\nbead init\nbead sync import-only --input .beads/checkpoint --restore-into-empty --actor \"$USER\"\nbead doctor\n```\n\n`bead doctor` runs read-only integrity checks across store, backup, schema,\ndependencies, and comments; `--repair` performs only safe, non-speculative\nrepairs, and `--rehearse` proves the recovery path by restoring into a throwaway\nworkspace and comparing the result for semantic equivalence.\n\n## Output contracts\n\n- `--json` on `list`, `changes`, and `query --output-json` emits **NDJSON** —\n  one compact object per line, not a JSON array.\n- `bead show --json` emits a **one-element array**, which is what NEEDLE's\n  subprocess contract expects.\n- `bead create` prints only the new bead ID and a newline, so it can be captured\n  directly into a shell variable.\n- `bead claim` on an empty frontier is success, not failure: exit 0 with `{}`.\n- `bead capabilities` emits a machine-readable contract document for feature\n  negotiation.\n\nExit codes are stable across every command:\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| 0 | Success |\n| 1 | Internal failure |\n| 2 | CLI usage or validation error |\n| 3 | Workspace, issue, or file not found |\n| 4 | Conflict — invalid transition, revision guard, dependency cycle, single-claim refusal |\n| 5 | Malformed input or integrity failure |\n\n## Coordinating a fleet\n\n![Many agents claiming from one ready frontier, backed by SQLite and a checkpoint](docs/img/how-bead-rs-works.png)\n\n- **Atomic claim.** Selection and assignment share one transaction under the\n  `fifo-v1` policy (priority ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC). `aging-v1`,\n  `impact-v1`, `rotation-v1`, and `balanced-v1` are also available via\n  `--policy`.\n- **Leases.** `bead claim --lease-ttl SECONDS` issues a lease with a\n  monotonically increasing fencing token, so a crashed or partitioned worker\n  cannot mutate work that has since been reassigned.\n- **Single-claim guard.** `bead claim --single-claim` refuses the claim when\n  the assignee already holds an `in_progress` issue in the workspace, failing\n  with exit 4 and reason code `assignee_has_active_claim` naming the blocking\n  issue. Opt-in per call, like `--lease-ttl`; it bounds claim accumulation but\n  does not detect stale claims — combine it with a lease TTL to bound how long\n  an abandoned claim can persist.\n- **Revision guards.** `--if-revision N` on `update`, `release`, `close`, and\n  `reopen` gives optimistic concurrency control; a stale revision fails with\n  exit 4 rather than silently losing an update.\n- **Inspect without reserving.** `bead list --ready` uses the same ordering as\n  `claim` but takes nothing off the frontier.\n- **Change feed.** `bead changes --since <CURSOR>` lets a consumer catch up\n  incrementally instead of rescanning.\n\n## Interoperability\n\nbead-rs keeps a private native schema. Per [ADR-002](docs/adr/002-agent-guided-rehydration-over-cross-tool-migration.md)\nit does not parse or transform another tool's checkpoint format:\n\n- `native-v1` — full fidelity, the default; the only supported recovery format\n- `needle-v1` — NEEDLE subprocess compatibility\n\n`bead compare --id <ID> --source <P> --target <P>` reports which fields a\ngiven profile pair preserves, transforms, omits, or cannot represent, scoped\nto these two profiles. Moving existing work from another tracker is\n**agent-guided rehydration**, not import: an agent reads the source\nrepository read-only and recreates work through public `bead` commands,\nproducing a reconciliation report rather than a synthesized checkpoint. See\n[interoperability notes](docs/notes/interoperability-architecture.md) and\n[NEEDLE compatibility](docs/notes/needle-compatibility.md).\n\n## CLI conventions worth knowing\n\nbead-rs is an independent implementation, not a drop-in replacement for any\nother task tracker. These conventions catch people out:\n\n| | |\n| --- | --- |\n| The binary is `bead` | not the crate name `bead-rs` |\n| `create` takes a flag | `bead create --title \"Title\"`, not a positional title |\n| Ready work is a filter | `bead list --ready`, not a `ready` command |\n| `flush-only` is a subcommand | `bead sync flush-only`, not `bead sync --flush-only` |\n| `--json` emits NDJSON | one object per line, not an array (except `show`, which emits a one-element array) |\n\n## Documentation\n\n- `bead --help` for the command inventory; `bead <COMMAND> --help` for the full\n  description, examples, and semantics of any command.\n- Man pages covering the whole command tree (45 pages, named `bead.1`,\n  `bead-create.1`, `bead-sync-flush-only.1`, …) are generated with\n  `cargo run --bin generate-man-pages`. See [MAN_PAGES.md](MAN_PAGES.md).\n- The [0.1 implementation plan](docs/plan/plan.md) defines the native schema,\n  lifecycle, dependency, checkpoint, CLI, and verification design.\n- Post-0.1 candidates and rejected alternatives live in the\n  [ideas ledger](docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md).\n\nBoth animations are generated from committed sources, so they can be refreshed\nrather than redrawn:\n\n```bash\n# lifecycle animation (needs cairosvg + Pillow)\npython3 docs/img/generate-lifecycle-animation.py\n\n# terminal screencast (needs vhs, which needs ttyd + ffmpeg)\ncargo install --path . && vhs docs/img/bead-workflow.tape\n```\n\nThe screencast drives the real binary, so it cannot quietly disagree with the\nCLI: if behaviour changes, re-running the tape either shows the change or\nvisibly fails.\n\nThe lifecycle animation is timed against the classical animation principles,\nused to carry meaning rather than decoration — the claim fires in 0.2s against\n0.4–0.6s elsewhere because atomicity is the point, and closing `design` sends a\nripple along the edge so that `store` turning ready reads as a consequence\nrather than a coincidence.\n\nIt also targets WCAG 2.1 AA. Every colour holding text clears 4.5:1 and every\nmeaningful graphic clears 3:1, asserted at generation time so the palette\ncannot regress; state is never colour-only, since each bead carries a text tag;\nthe animation plays a fixed number of times rather than looping forever; and a\n`prefers-reduced-motion` source serves the static storyboard instead. Emphasis\nis carried by scale and stroke weight rather than by dimming, because a dim\ndeep enough to read as staging takes text below the contrast floor. The\ngenerator documents both mappings in full.\n\nEvery `bead ...` example printed in the help text is parsed by the real CLI in\nthe test suite, so a documented invocation cannot drift from the interface it\ndocuments.\n\n## Project status\n\nThe core CLI is implemented and in use: workspace lifecycle, issue CRUD,\nlabels, the dependency graph, atomic and leased claims, checkpoint flush and\nrestore, diagnostics, the query language, the change feed, profiles, and\nmigration. It has been exercised end to end by building a real multi-bead\nproject through it.\n\nTreat it as young software rather than settled: it is a 0.1, its history\nincludes bugs that a green test suite did not catch, and it is worth running\n`bead doctor` and a hands-on smoke test of the path you care about before\ndepending on it for anything critical.\n\n## Independence\n\n`bead-rs` has an independent Git history and is implemented from the\nspecifications committed to this repository. Clean-room contributors must\nfollow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md).\n\n`bead-rs` is not affiliated with or endorsed by any other bead implementation.\n\n## License\n\nApache License 2.0.
